gloss: shiatsu — a Japanese form of therapeutic massage using finger pressure on acupressure points along the body

definitions.gloss: shiatsu — a Japanese therapeutic massage technique using thumbs, fingers, and palms to apply pressure to points along the body
definitions.explanation: A Japanese therapeutic technique in which the practitioner applies pressure — primarily with the thumbs, fingers, and palms — to specific points along the body. {指圧|しあつ} draws on traditional East Asian medical theory of meridians ({経絡|けいらく}) and pressure points ({ツボ}), but became codified as a distinct modality in early twentieth-century Japan and is now licensed alongside acupuncture and anma massage. The same word is used internationally as the loanword "shiatsu."

examples.japanese: {肩|かた}{こり}には{指圧|しあつ}が{効|き}く。
examples.english: Shiatsu is effective for stiff shoulders.

examples.japanese: {指圧|しあつ}{師|し}に{腰|こし}の{痛|いた}みを{相談|そうだん}した。
examples.english: I consulted a shiatsu practitioner about my back pain.

examples.japanese: {指圧|しあつ}は{経絡|けいらく}と呼ばれる{流|なが}れに{沿|そ}って{身体|しんたい}のツボに{圧|あつ}を{加|くわ}え、{血行|けっこう}や{自然|しぜん}{治癒|ちゆ}{力|りょく}を{高|たか}めるとされている。
examples.english: Shiatsu applies pressure to points on the body along channels called meridians and is said to improve blood circulation and the body's natural healing ability.

notes:
{指圧|しあつ} is a Japanese form of therapeutic massage in which the practitioner uses fingers, thumbs, and palms to apply pressure to acupressure points along the body. It is internationally known as "shiatsu."

FORMATION:
- {指|し} ("finger") + {圧|あつ} ("pressure") → {指圧|しあつ} "finger pressure"
- A modern Sino-Japanese coinage codifying a traditional bodywork practice.

PRACTICE AND REGULATION:
- Developed and codified as a distinct technique in early-twentieth-century Japan, building on older anma ({あん}{摩|ま}) massage and Chinese acupressure traditions.
- Practitioners are typically licensed as {あん}{摩|ま}{マッサージ}{指圧|しあつ}{師|し} ("anma-massage-shiatsu practitioner") under Japanese law.
- Sessions are typically performed on a futon or mat with the client clothed (no oil), making {指圧|しあつ} distinct from oil-based Western massage.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {指圧|しあつ}を{受|う}ける: to receive a shiatsu treatment
- {指圧|しあつ}を{する}: to give a shiatsu treatment / to massage with finger pressure
- {指圧|しあつ}{師|し}: shiatsu practitioner
- {指圧|しあつ}{院|いん}: shiatsu clinic
- ツボを{指圧|しあつ}する: to press on an acupressure point
- {指圧|しあつ}が{効|き}く: shiatsu is effective (for a condition)

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- マッサージ: massage (general loanword) — broader and often refers to Western-style oil massage
- {あん}{摩|ま}: anma — traditional Japanese massage; the older sibling of shiatsu, also licensed alongside it
- {鍼|はり}: acupuncture (needle therapy) — uses needles instead of finger pressure; same underlying meridian theory
- {灸|きゅう}: moxibustion — burning moxa on points; same meridian theory
- {整体|せいたい}: a Japanese style of bodywork emphasizing structural alignment; overlaps with but is distinct from shiatsu
- {ツボ}: acupressure point — the spots that shiatsu and acupuncture target
- {経絡|けいらく}: meridian — the channels along which pressure points are arranged in traditional theory
- {リフレクソロジー}: reflexology — Western-style foot pressure-point therapy

USAGE NOTES:
- {指圧|しあつ} is a noun; the corresponding verb is {指圧|しあつ}する.
- For everyday "please rub my shoulders," Japanese speakers more often say {肩|かた}を{揉|も}んで rather than the more clinical {指圧|しあつ}して.
- Shiatsu as a Western loanword is spelled "shiatsu" in many languages, with the same meaning as in Japanese.
